decision: Use the technical SEO matrix as the page-type contract before building or indexing routes.
implementation_spec: Every route type gets index policy, canonical rule, robots rule, sitemap rule, hreflang rule, schema, breadcrumb, and noindex conditions.
why_this_way: Mass page creation without a route matrix creates duplicate, thin, or conflicting pages.
acceptance_gate: Every build PR maps new routes to a page_id row before release.

decision: Every indexable page gets one self canonical; duplicate/filter/thin variants canonicalize or noindex according to the matrix.
implementation_spec: Do not mix canonical signals with robots blocks that prevent Google from seeing the canonical.
why_this_way: Canonical rules prevent cannibalization and duplicate city/filter pages.
acceptance_gate: Crawl sample proves canonical URL matches page map.

decision: Use robots meta noindex for page-level exclusion; do not use robots.txt as a noindex mechanism.
implementation_spec: Thin filters, unverified listings, missing assets, legal-unreviewed pages, and country-abroad drafts get noindex until gates pass.
why_this_way: Google does not support noindex in robots.txt, and page-level control is safer.
acceptance_gate: Rendered head shows correct robots rule for sample index/noindex pages.

decision: Only canonical, approved, indexable URLs belong in public XML and HTML sitemaps.
implementation_spec: Exclude placeholders, noindex pages, unverified listings, internal admin/report pages, and country-abroad drafts.
why_this_way: Sitemaps should describe important canonical pages, not every generated URL.
acceptance_gate: Sitemap sample contains only indexable canonical URLs and passes Search Console after deploy.

decision: Use structured data only when it matches visible content and source truth.
implementation_spec: Organization/WebSite on home; BreadcrumbList on navigable pages; ItemList on hubs; Product/Offer only for real visible offers; Professional/LocalBusiness only for verified professionals.
why_this_way: Structured data that invents facts can harm trust and rich result eligibility.
acceptance_gate: Rich Results Test screenshots or exports exist for each P0 template.

decision: Prevent duplicate schema from theme, plugins, and custom code.
implementation_spec: One schema owner per page type. Yoast/plugin schema must be audited before adding custom JSON-LD.
why_this_way: Conflicting Organization, Breadcrumb, Product, or Offer markup confuses search engines.
acceptance_gate: Rendered HTML scan shows one intended schema graph per template.

decision: Breadcrumbs must be visible where useful and marked with BreadcrumbList when page hierarchy is stable.
implementation_spec: Use the canonical page hierarchy, not the user’s filter path, as the structured breadcrumb.
why_this_way: Breadcrumbs clarify IA and reduce duplicate path ambiguity.
acceptance_gate: Breadcrumb Rich Results Test passes on representative page types.

decision: Use hreflang only between true alternate language pages with matching intent.
implementation_spec: Do not create hreflang for partial translations, automatic translations, or pages with different intent.
why_this_way: Bad hreflang can create canonical confusion in the English investor layer.
acceptance_gate: Crawl sample shows reciprocal language alternates and self canonicals.

decision: Product/Offer markup is allowed only when price, availability, currency, and source are visible and current.
implementation_spec: No fake prices, no fake availability, no implied unit offer when inventory is missing.
why_this_way: Project and listing pages are commercial, but schema must not claim more than the page proves.
acceptance_gate: Offer markup sample passes validation and matches screenshot.

decision: Most filter/sort URLs should be noindex unless they become approved canonical pages.
implementation_spec: City and neighborhood hubs can index after supply gates; arbitrary filters remain noindex/canonicalized.
why_this_way: Filters can create thousands of duplicate or thin pages.
acceptance_gate: Crawl proves filter URLs do not enter sitemap and carry correct robots/canonical.

decision: Project and showroom pages cannot index until source and asset truth gates pass.
implementation_spec: If GLB, floor plan, view, inventory, or price is missing, the page must show an honest state and avoid unsupported schema.
why_this_way: The showroom is high-value, but fake asset pages create legal and trust risk.
acceptance_gate: Screenshot shows asset truth and rendered structured data matches it.

decision: English pages index only after source, legal, hreflang, and language quality gates pass.
implementation_spec: /en pages are written for foreign buyers; country-abroad pages remain noindex until local source packs exist.
why_this_way: This protects Hebrew authority while building international demand.
acceptance_gate: /en sample pages pass language, canonical, hreflang, and screenshot gates.

decision: Use Search Console evidence after deployment: sitemap status, URL Inspection, page indexing, enhancements, and canonical reports.
implementation_spec: Repo screenshots are not enough for final technical SEO clearance.
why_this_way: Search Console is the source for Google’s indexed/crawled state.
acceptance_gate: Post-deploy evidence file links sample URL inspections and sitemap status.

decision: No new page family ships without technical SEO checklist and screenshots.
implementation_spec: Checklist includes title, H1, canonical, robots, sitemap, schema, breadcrumbs, internal links, mobile, console errors, and visible language.
why_this_way: This prevents visual work from shipping with broken indexation.
acceptance_gate: Release packet includes crawl output, screenshots, and matrix row references.
